resolutions.finding: MCPProxy.swift:103 allowLocalEndpointReuse must not become SO_REUSEADDR on Windows
resolutions.truth: Line 103 is `parameters.allowLocalEndpointReuse = true`. Lines 9-11 say 'the second to launch would answer nothing' and lines 96-98 say a taken port 'fails only once the listener starts', so the design relies on a second bind failing. Winsock SO_REUSEADDR lets a second socket bind a port that is in use, so a literal mapping would never detect the collision. Added to platform_assumptions with EADDRINUSE as the re-pick trigger.

resolutions.finding: MCPProxy.swift:315 timeoutInterval 3_600 is an idle timeout, not a total deadline
resolutions.truth: Line 315 is `request.timeoutInterval = 3_600` on a URLRequest sent with `URLSession.shared.bytes(for:)` (344/349). URLRequest.timeoutInterval is the inactivity interval between data. The total cap is the session's timeoutIntervalForResource. Added to side_effects and platform_assumptions with a warning against AbortSignal.timeout(3600000).

resolutions.finding: MCPProxy.swift:376-387 + 403-408: the upstream is never cancelled when the client disconnects in the middle of SSE
resolutions.truth: send (403-408) is `connection.send(content: data, completion: .contentProcessed { _ in continuation.resume() })` and ignores the error. The SSE loop `for try await byte in stream { ... await send(connection, frame) }` (377-382) has no client-close check, and nothing receives on the connection after the body is read. The loop therefore runs until the upstream ends or throws. Consequence added to the send note.

resolutions.finding: MCPProxy.swift:193-202: the divider check runs before the size check, so heads larger than 64 KiB are accepted
resolutions.truth: `if let divider = buffer.range(of: Self.divider) {... return}` (193-198) comes before `if buffer.count > Self.headLimit {... 413 ...}` (199-202). Each receive has `maximumLength: Self.headLimit` (184). A buffer of at most 65_536 bytes can therefore grow to 131_072 bytes and still be accepted, so the exact maximum head is 131_068 bytes (the critic's figure was about 131_071). Added to the readHead note.

resolutions.finding: MCPProxy.swift:389-392: the non-SSE response is buffered with no size limit
resolutions.truth: Lines 389-392 are `var payload = Data()` / `for try await byte in stream { payload.append(byte) }` with no cap. bodyLimit (`32 * 1_024 * 1_024`, line 50) is checked only at line 241, `if contentLength > Self.bodyLimit`, which applies to the request body.

resolutions.finding: MCPProxy.swift:344-352: when the retry token fetch fails, the original 401 is passed back; the first stream is not drained; no forced refresh

resolutions.finding: StreamVeil.swift:423-426 - AppKit veil uses withAlphaComponent, which replaces alpha rather than multiplying; dimmed runs (labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.7)) ramp toward 1.0 and drop back to 0.7 on settle

NSColor ?? .labelColor)` then `layout.addTemporaryAttribute(.foregroundColor, value: color.withAlphaComponent(span.alpha), forCharacterRange: runRange)`. The span alpha becomes the run's absolute alpha. B2 LinkParagraphView.swift:121 `let textColor = dimmed ? NSColor.labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.7) : NSColor.labelColor`, applied as .foregroundColor at lines 143/152. So a dimmed fading run goes from 0 up toward 1.0, and clear() (line 405 removeTemporaryAttribute) brings it back to 0.7. resolutions.finding: StreamVeil.swift:311,319 - SwiftUI Color.opacity on Color.primary.opacity(0.7) multiplies, so dimmed veiled SwiftUI runs peak at 0.7*alpha, unlike the AppKit path
resolutions.truth: Line 311 `let base = dimmed ? Color.primary.opacity(0.7) : Color.primary`, and line 319 `styled[lower..<upper].foregroundColor = base.opacity(span.alpha)`. SwiftUI Color.opacity multiplies the colour's existing opacity, so a dimmed run's effective opacity is 0.7*alpha. The AppKit path sets an absolute alpha instead (line 426). The report's ui_elements and purpose now state both behaviours and the difference.

resolutions.finding: StreamVeil.swift:110-113 with 171-193 - settlesAt uses the boost for the current chunk count and can come before the true settle; upstream relies on tick tearing down the link and fadingText re-arming it
resolutions.truth: Lines 111-112: `let boost = Self.boost(chunks.count)` then `return chunks.map { $0.started.addingTimeInterval($0.duration / boost) }.max()`. prune (125-126) and spans (89-90) recompute boost from the smaller count after pruning, so the remaining chunks slow down. tick (188-192) runs `now = .now`, then `guard let deadline, now >= deadline`, then `link?.invalidate(); link = nil; self.deadline = nil`. The re-render calls fadingText, whose line 286 `clock.run(until: settlesAt)` passes `guard link == nil` (line 173) and creates a new link. Line 172 `deadline = max(deadline ?? date, date)` also re-extends the deadline on every fading render. The re-arm requirement was added to the settlesAt feature_note.

resolutions.finding: StreamVeil.swift:274 vs 284-288 - body and fadingText read Date.now separately, and spans prunes again, so the fading branch can render with fewer spans; LinkTextVeil.update uses one timestamp

LinkTextVeil.update line 355 `let now = Date.now` is used for both step (356) and paint (357). This was added to the fadingText feature_note.

resolutions.finding: AppTheme.swift:241-242: 'unparseable string yields 0 (black)' is only true when the first char is not hex; scanHexInt64 keeps the hex prefix, accepts 0x/0X, and gives UInt64.max on overflow
resolutions.truth: Line 241 `var value: UInt64 = 0`, line 242 `Scanner(string: text).scanHexInt64(&value)` (Bool result ignored), lines 243-245 take (value >> 16)&0xFF, (value >> 8)&0xFF, value&0xFF. Foundation scanHexInt64 parses the leading hex digits, accepts an optional 0x/0X prefix and stores UInt64.max on overflow, so "12GG34" gives blue 0x12, more than 16 hex digits gives white, and only a string starting with a non-hex char (or an empty one) gives black. All palette literals on lines 114-139 are 6-digit hex.
